comparisons.peer_summary: Depreciation expense for property, plant, and equipment was $7.70 billion in 2024, $7.67 billion in 2023, and $7.03 billion in 2022. Additionally, interest capitalized as part of the cost of these assets amounted to $225 million in 2024, $208 million in 2023, and $77 million in 2022.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel (INTC) reported specific non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation totaling over $3.2 billion due to excess manufacturing capacity at the Intel 7 node, Micron (MU) reported significantly higher standard depreciation expense ($7.70 billion) but did not disclose similar large-scale impairment charges for property, plant, and equipment in this specific disclosure. Both companies are semiconductor manufacturers reporting on PP&E details, but Intel's disclosure is characterized by significant asset write-downs driven by capacity assessments, whereas MU's disclosure focuses on the magnitude of ongoing depreciation and capitalized interest without mentioning impairments in the cited text.

sentences.text: In connection with the preparation of our Consolidated Financial Statements for the third quarter of 2024, we evaluated our current process technology node capacities relative to projected market demand for our products and services, and concluded that our manufacturing asset portfolio, primarily for our Intel 7 process node, exceeded manufacturing capacity requirements.

In total, we recorded non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation charges of $2.3 billion and $992 million, respectively, in 2024, substantially all of which were recognized in cost of sales within our Intel Foundry operating segment.
Depreciation expense was $7.70 billion, $7.67 billion, and $7.03 billion for 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
Interest capitalized as part of the cost of property, plant, and equipment was $225 million, $208 million, and $77 million for 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
